title: Predictive soft-quota orchestration for mixed weights/KV/activation footprints
creator: Ethan Morales
description: Design and implement a predictive "soft-quota" coordinator that dynamically budgets GPU memory across model weights, KV cache, and runtime activations. The coordinator should provide a small predictive headroom buffer that adapts to sequence-length and tenancy variance, enabling more aggressive continuous batching while maintaining SLOs (P99 latency and OOM avoidance). This ticket covers design, simulator validation, a conservative canary rollout, and console telemetry for operations and alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator exposes a per-GPU memory budget split (weights | kv | activations | headroom) via agent config and runtime API
Simulator shows >= 8% cost improvement (measured as tokens/sec per GPU hour) for mixed workloads vs static quotas without increasing P99 latency by >5%
No regressions in OOM events in canary region and gradual rollout plan documented
Console dashboard surfaces 'soft-quota pressure' and headroom consumption metrics; alerts for sustained headroom < 10%
Integration tests covering eviction, preemption zapping, and graceful fallback to conservative quotas pass in CI
design_notes:
High-level approach:
- Rationale: static quotas allocate a fixed slice to KV vs activations and fail to capture burstiness from sequence length and tenant co-tenancy. We introduce a lightweight coordinator that forecasts short-horizon demand and issues temporary soft-quotas plus an elastic headroom token pool.
- Forecasting: EWMA of per-model sequence-length distribution + tenant burst indicator derived from recent request size percentiles (90/95/99) and arrival-rate derivative. Use a small LRU-weighted window (30s) for rapid adaptation.
- Allocation primitives:
  1) Hard-reserve for static weights (non-evictable) always pinned.
  2) Soft-quota buckets for KV and activations (evictable with priority). Soft quotas can be borrowed from the headroom token pool when predicted safe.
  3) Headroom token pool: a dynamically sized buffer (percentage of free GPU memory) computed from forecast quantile (e.g., 99th percentile demand delta) and a safety multiplier.
  4) Stitching: when multiple models/tenants' KV interact, the coordinator performs KV 'stitch' estimation to avoid cascading evictions — prefer compacting older KV segments first and enforce an upper bound on KV growth per-tenant.
- Eviction policy integration: tie soft-quota pressure to the existing KV eviction controller and activation preemption hooks. Under sustained pressure beyond safety bounds, trigger graceful shedding: reduce batching window for non-critical tenants, and enable KV segment compression (lossy quantization) if configured.
- Canary & safety: default controller is conservative (small headroom). Provide tunables: response-sensitivity, safety-multiplier, min-headroom-fraction. Start canary on a dedicated pool with telemetry gating.
- Rollback: automatic disable to static quotas on repeated OOM or if headroom < 5% for > 120s.
- Observability: expose metrics: predicted_demand_percentile, headroom_tokens, borrowed_headroom, soft_quota_hits, evictions_triggered_by_soft_quota, batch_window_ms, canary_health. Include traces for allocation decisions.
- API: /agent/v1/memory-coordinator GET/PUT for runtime overrides and manual disable.
- Performance budget: coordinator must add <1.5ms median overhead per allocation decision and scale at 10k req/s per GPU host.
- Security: no persistent customer data stored; only aggregated telemetry sent to control plane.
tasks: Simulator: extend mem-sim to model mixed-weight/KV/activation footprints and headroom policies (branch: github.com/redwood-inference/mem-sim/tree/soft-quota)
KV integration: add soft-quota hooks into kv-evictor module and implement stitching heuristics
E2E tests: fault-injection tests for OOM scenarios and preemption path
Canary rollout: deploy to canary-pool, instrument dashboards and SLO checks
Docs & Runbook: write operator runbook for alert response and rollback steps
Performance tuning: microbench the decision path and optimize locking/contention
